name: retention_logical_clock
invariant: INV-5 / §3.5 — retention ages the journal on the WIRE's logical clock (`edit_time`, fixed-width UTC per INV-6), not the row's physical arrival time
notes: Website-side extension of the frozen `tombstone_survives_prune` vector. That vector uses `keep_days = 0`, which drops a just-inserted row under EITHER clock, so it cannot tell `edit_time`-based retention from `created_at`-based retention. The app's `prune_log` ages rows on `edit_time` (`sync/change_log.rs:424,444 — WHERE datetime(edit_time) < datetime('now', ?1)`); a website that instead aged on `created_at` would keep a freshly-arrived old edit forever and hand followers different usable history than the desktop hub for the same journal. This vector pins the difference: a row whose `edit_time` is decades old but which was inserted moments ago MUST be pruned at `keep_days = 30`, raising `pruned_up_to` so the cursor-below-the-mark follower is told `resync_required`. A row with no parsable `edit_time` is never pruned (the app's SQLite `datetime('')` = NULL semantics), which the companion harness guard checks.
